summary: Exact candidate 03db4be879e92bb6f85cb1fcd9d571346a9028bc is a correct partial implementation. It changes single-rank composed-pipeline scheduling from sequential to concurrent, preserves deterministic assembly and failure propagation, provides an opt-out, and serializes unsafe complete Transformers/Diffusers native loads. The original base failure was independently reproduced and the candidate passed focused, adversarial, compatibility, and one-GPU synthetic numerical tests. It does not demonstrate the reported Qwen-Image speedup or implement the original issue's wake/refit and pinned-checkpoint goals.

tests.what_was_measured: Original sequential behavior reproduced: three independent 0.2-second component loads reached max_active=1 and took 0.603 seconds.
Candidate scheduling overlapped all three independent loads: max_active=3 and elapsed time 0.204 seconds, while preserving component order.
32 focused scheduler, thread-safety, CLI, failure, ordering, loader compatibility, and GPU regression tests passed.
Actual Transformers 5.12.1 local_torch_dtype contexts observed their requested dtypes and restored the process default.
Expected counterexample/limitation: two complete native loads did not overlap (max_active_native_loads=1, 0.401 seconds for two 0.2-second calls).
On one AMD Instinct MI350X, synthetic concurrently loaded GPU Linear modules matched independent NumPy references; this does not validate Qwen-Image semantics or startup time.
Extended compatibility: 68 passed and 9 subtests passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) was visible under torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015. The synthetic GPU numerical regression passed against NumPy. No Qwen-Image weights were available.

remaining_counterexamples: Complete native Transformers/Diffusers load_native calls are serialized for correctness, so two native components do not overlap.
The reported Qwen-Image 63.20-second module-load bottleneck and launch-time reduction remain unmeasured with real weights.
Sleep/wake restoration and post-training refit paths are unchanged and untested.
Production checkpoint mappings remain pageable; pinned checkpoint loading is not implemented or validated.
Multi-rank component loading remains sequential by design.
Peak host memory and storage pressure are neither automatically bounded nor measured with representative checkpoints.
remaining_limitations: The result verifies a partial initial-load scheduler and its native thread-safety correction, not the complete original feature contract.
Qwen-Image weights were unavailable in the prepared runtime, preventing representative cold-start, CPU-memory, storage-pressure, and semantic checks.
The available architecture was one AMD Instinct MI350X; no CUDA/NVIDIA execution was possible.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable. The prepared AIter shared object imported from /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-60f8fe608a12/cache/aiter/module_aiter_core.so.
